title: Sandboxed rollback orchestra notes and light playbook
body:
Context
---
Personal scratchpad for a lightweight, sandboxed rollback choreography we talked about in the release ops sync. Idea: treat each rollback as a small orchestra with short, deterministic cues rather than a big hammer. Keep producer (client routing) and consumer (inference pool) actions separate and observable.

Goals / constraints
- Minimize blast radius for user-visible latency regressions and hallucination spikes.
- Fast, reversible actions that are automatable but with human-in-the-loop confirmation for critical paths.
- Keep cost/throughput disruptions small (prefer partial traffic drains over full drains).
- Reuse existing Falcon routing primitives and flagging infra where possible.

Core primitives (mental model)
1) Pin: lock a cohort to a model hash/version (no autopromote). Good for long investigations.
2) Holdback bucket: route X% of traffic to a stable previous variant (non-optimized path).
3) Decant: move small cohorts off the new variant into shadow/stable for extended observation.
4) Throttle/attenuate: reduce max tokens or force lower concurrency for affected cohorts to throttle cost and tail latency.
5) Orchestration cue: single command that emits a high-fidelity event to routing, monitoring, and incident channel.

Quick operational checklist (for quiet hours or staged incidents)
- Pre-step (10m): confirm owner, incident channel, and primary metric targets. Notify on-call and product PM.
- Safety snapshot: capture baseline (P50/P95/P99 latency, error rate, token cost, top 10 client ids by qps) for the last 15 minutes.
- Canary holdback flip (2-5m): move 3–5% from variant:new -> variant:stable (use routing flag). Verify traffic counts.
- Observe (5–15m): P95 and error spikes. If metrics worsen > threshold, escalate to rollback.
- Rollback (2m): run orchestrated command that does: pin stable for effected cohorts, reduce concurrency to 50% on new variant, create incident note.
- Postmortem plan: keep the pin for 24–72h (depending on severity) while triage proceeds.

Heuristics / thresholds (first-pass)
- Latency: P95 increase > 30% over baseline OR absolute P95 > 800ms -> immediate action.
- Errors: 5xx + client error rate increase > 1% absolute -> evaluate rollback.
- Quality: model quality regression on eval set (automated scoring) drop > 3% (precision/recall proxy) -> holdback.
- Token cost: unit cost > 20% increase -> throttle recommendations.

Sample commands / pseudo-ops (notes to self)
- flag flip: ./infra/routectl set-cohort --cohort "legacy-users" --from model:v2 --to model:v1 --percent 5 --reason "latency spike test"
- pin: ./infra/modelctl pin --model model:v1 --cohort "checkout-flows" --ttl 72h --owner carter
- attenuate: ./infra/servectl set-qps --model model:v2 --cohort "high-latency" --qps 50
- query telemetry: ./telemetry/query --metrics p95,p99,err_rate --since 15m --cohorts "all"

Observability shortcuts (what I watch in first 10 minutes)
- P95 by cohort (sorted): sudden jumpers flagged
- Error rate/timeouts: rolling 5m and 1m windows
- Request tail size (tokens > 1024): see if new variant increases long-run queries
- Token cost burn rate: compare to last hour and last deploy period

Rollback choreography options (in decreasing severity)
1) Micro rollback: shift 5–10% back to stable cohort by routing flag. Keep new variant running for diagnostics.
2) Quarantine: pin affected cohorts to stable and leave remaining traffic on new for targeted apps.
3) Throttle + shadow: limit concurrency and shadow requests to new variant for sampling.
4) Full rollback: replace default route with stable model and scale down new variant to zero. Document reason and notify.

Decision matrix (quick look)
- Is the issue localized to a small cohort? -> Micro rollback or quarantine.
- Is it global latency degradation but minimal error increase? -> Throttle + holdback, observe 30m.
- Is it catastrophic error (client-facing error spike)? -> Full rollback + incident bridge.

Notes about pins and rollbacks
- Pins are cheap but contagious: once pinned, clients might cache and delay resolution. Avoid pinning > 72h without trade-off approval.
- Always attach a TTL and owner metadata to any pin. Use template: "pin:<owner>:<reason>:<expiry>"
- Record the exact commit/model-hash and serving infra id for reproducibility (use the snapshot script).

Open questions / TODOs (short list)
- Can we automate the 5% micro rollback as a single button in Console with pre-filled playbook steps? (low effort, high value)
- Should we add an automated audio/visual cue in the incident bridge when safety thresholds are crossed?
- Explore implementing an ephemeral "sandbox" routing namespace that mirrors live traffic but cannot be promoted for 24h.
- Need a small runbook for SDK-driven flips (safety validation + canary percent limits).

Post-incident template (notes to add after any rollback)
1) Timestamp of rollback command + operator
2) What was shifted (cohorts + percent)
3) Telemetry snapshot before and after (p95/p99/errors/cost)
4) Root cause hypothesis and next steps for engineering
5) If pinned, plan and date for unpin

Personal reminders
- Keep playbook terse; engineers copy/paste. Avoid long prose in hot paths.
- Prefer reversible small moves over large irreversible changes.
- When in doubt, throttle + observe.

End of scratchpad.

(If this lands in a more formal doc later: convert heuristics to SLO-backed thresholds and add automation tests for micro rollback safety.)
